tieu_de: Why does Spain own two cities in Africa?
chu_de: Why does Spain own two cities in Africa?

cau.chu: Spain still owns two small cities on African soil today.

su_that.trich: Ceuta (UK: , US: ; Spanish: [ˈθewta, ˈsewta] ; Moroccan Arabic: سَبْتَة, romanized: Sabtah) is an autonomous city of Spain on the North African coast.

Melilla (, Spanish: [meˈliʝa] ; Tarifit: Mřič) is an autonomous city of Spain on the North African coast. It lies on the eastern side of the Cape Three Forks, on the Morocco–Spain border, adjacent to the Moroccan port town of Beni Ansar, and faces the Mediterranean Sea.

cau.chu: They are Ceuta and Melilla, hugging the coast of Morocco.

su_that.trich: Ceuta (UK: , US: ; Spanish: [ˈθewta, ˈsewta] ; Moroccan Arabic: سَبْتَة, romanized: Sabtah) is an autonomous city of Spain on the North African coast.

Melilla (, Spanish: [meˈliʝa] ; Tarifit: Mřič) is an autonomous city of Spain on the North African coast. It lies on the eastern side of the Cape Three Forks, on the Morocco–Spain border, adjacent to the Moroccan port town of Beni Ansar, and faces the Mediterranean Sea.

cau.chu: In fourteen fifteen, Portugal stormed Ceuta with forty five thousand men.

su_that.trich: On the morning of 21 August 1415, King John I of Portugal led his sons and their assembled forces in a surprise assault that would come to be known as the Conquest of Ceuta.
The 45,000 Portuguese who traveled on 200 ships caught the defenders of Ceuta off guard and suffered only eight casualties.

cau.chu: Portugal held the city for more than two centuries.

su_that.trich: In 1580, it was annexed by the Hispanic Monarchy, and the city chose to remain under Spanish authority after 1640.

cau.chu: Then in sixteen forty, Portugal broke free and Ceuta chose Madrid.

su_that.trich: During the Hispanic Monarchy, which lasted from 1580 to 1640, Ceuta attracted many residents of mainland Spanish origin and eventually became the only city in the Portuguese Empire that sided with Madrid when Portugal regained its independence in the Portuguese Restoration War of 1640–1668.

cau.chu: On New Year's Day sixteen sixty eight, Lisbon signed Ceuta away for good.

su_that.trich: On 1 January 1668, King Afonso VI of Portugal recognised the formal allegiance of Ceuta to Spain and ceded Ceuta to King Carlos II of Spain by the Treaty of Lisbon.
On 1 January 1668, King Afonso VI of Portugal recognised the formal allegiance of Ceuta to Spain and ceded Ceuta to King Carlos II of Spain by the Treaty of Lisbon.

cau.chu: Melilla fell in fourteen ninety seven, almost without a fight.

su_that.trich: Melilla was occupied on 17 September 1497, virtually without violence as it was on the border between the Kingdom of Tlemcen and the Kingdom of Fez, and as a result had been fought over many times and left abandoned.

cau.chu: Morocco besieged Ceuta for thirty three years, the longest siege in history.

su_that.trich: The city was attacked by Moroccan forces under Moulay Ismail during the Siege of Ceuta (1694–1727), the longest siege in history.

cau.chu: Spain held both fortresses through every siege and every treaty.

su_that.trich: When Spain recognized the independence of Spanish Morocco in 1956, Ceuta and the other plazas de soberanía remained under Spanish rule.

cau.chu: But Morocco claims both cities to this day, and the fight is still open. That's part two.

su_that.trich: Like the autonomous city of Ceuta and Spain's other territories along the northern African coast, Melilla is subject to an irredentist claim by Morocco.
